title: Can one move replace two?
action: Drive the two-wheel chassis along two straight legs. Track its centre, leave a bent trail, then put a hollow ring around its finish. Withhold the direct arrow.
cue: Ask whether one command could reach the same ring. Leave a prediction beat.
math: The first displacement is (3, 1) and the second is (−1, 2). The finish is marked without revealing its coordinates.

title: Three views of one move
action: Replay the first leg. Its trail becomes an arrow. Keep it visible while the calculation area moves from controller to floor to algebra, with a brief inventory example.
cue: Describe the same command as an ordered pair, a directed displacement and an object that can be added or scaled.
math: u = (3, 1) gives changes in world x and y. An inventory pair (4, 2) counts wheels and sensors in a specified order.

title: Read the change
action: Reveal dashed horizontal and vertical measures. Copy their numbers into a column. Slide a duplicate of the solid arrow to a new tail, keeping the first arrow visible.
cue: Ask why the new tip has a different address while the command is unchanged.
math: New tail (−2, 1), new tip (1, 2). Tip minus tail gives (1 − (−2), 2 − 1) = (3, 1).

title: Put the moves together
action: Slide a solid coral copy from the origin to the teal tip. Drive the robot along both arrows. Hold the bent path, then join start and end with a gold arrow. Reveal horizontal and vertical totals.
cue: Read the horizontal cancellation and the two upward contributions. Compare net displacement with distance along the route.
math: u + v = (3 − 1, 1 + 2) = (2, 3). Both trips have the same endpoints; the direct path is shorter.

title: Scale and combine
action: Drive the slider through one, one half, zero, negative one and two. Replace the vanishing active arrow with a dot. Finish with a prediction and a half-length teal arrow plus the full coral arrow.
cue: Explain reversal and the length factor. Pause before constructing half the first move plus all of the second.
math: ku = (3k, k). At k = −1 the tip is (−3, −1); at k = 2 it is (6, 2). Half u plus v gives (0.5, 2.5).

title: One command to the ring
action: Restore the bent trail and goal ring. Move the robot directly along the growing gold arrow. Hold its centre on the ring while the three takeaways and credits appear.
cue: Watch the centre meet the ring. Recall displacement, addition of successive moves and componentwise scaling.
math: The single command (2, 3) reproduces the two-command displacement. Scaled commands can be added to create a linear combination.
